title.en: Solve ax² + bx + c = 0 when D < 0

say.en: Earlier we stopped at "no real roots". With i we can now solve every quadratic equation. In this lesson: Solve ax squared plus bx plus c equals 0 when D is less than 0.
Use the conjugate-pair property.

body.en: For $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ with real $a, b, c$ and $a \ne 0$, $D = b^2 - 4ac$. If $D < 0$, the roots are $x = \dfrac{-b \pm i\sqrt{4ac - b^2}}{2a}$, a pair of *complex* conjugates. A polynomial equation of degree $n$ has $n$ roots (counted in the complex numbers).
body.kn: D = b² − 4ac < 0 ಆದಾಗ ಮೂಲಗಳು (−b ± i√(4ac − b²))/2a; ಅವು ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಸಂಯುಗ್ಮ ಸಂಕೀರ್ಣ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಗಳು.

points.en: Real coefficients ⇒ non-real *roots* come in conjugate pairs

narration.en: When the discriminant is negative, the square root of D becomes i times the square root of minus D. The two roots are complex conjugates of each other.

say.en: When the discriminant is negative, the square root of D becomes i times the square root of minus D. The two roots are complex conjugates of each other. Sum of roots equals -b over a, product equals c over a.
say.kn: D equals b squared minus 4ac is less than 0 ಆದಾಗ ಮೂಲಗಳು (-b plus or minus i the square root of (4ac - b squared))/2a; ಅವು ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಸಂಯುಗ್ಮ ಸಂಕೀರ್ಣ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಗಳು.

a equals 1, b equals 1, c equals 1; D equals 1 minus 4 equals minus 3.

heading.en: Build the equation from one complex root

body.en: If p + iq is a root with real coefficients, so is p − iq. The equation is x² − 2p·x + (p² + q²) = 0: sum 2p, product p² + q².
